o1.biggest_strength: Makes the face wash + serum pair bundle one at a modest ₹869. Every profit figure includes the ₹70 shipping and the expected RTO cost, and the working is shown so I can check it.
o1.biggest_mistake: Lip balm, the natural ₹199 add-on, is not used as a bundle or cart add-on, and there is no COD-only threshold or prepaid nudge, even though RTO is in the maths.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Swap the serum pair for a lip-balm cart add-on to cross the line, and add a COD-specific rule such as free shipping at ₹599 for prepaid only.

o2.biggest_strength: A clear price ladder on the serum page and a well-argued case against a plain duo discount that would just give money away on 1,033 existing orders.
o2.biggest_mistake: The ₹599 threshold maths rests on an unsupported guess that only 6% of orders sit between ₹499 and ₹598, when my 27% band suggests nearer 13%. Profit figures also leave out RTO cost, so the threshold verdict is shaky.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Size the affected orders from the real band data, put COD refusal cost into every profit line, and use lip balm as a cart add-on instead of a main bundle.

reason: Both pick ₹599 and a sensible test plan. Output 1 builds bundle one on my top pair, counts refusals in every number, and sizes the threshold change from my own data. Output 2's threshold case leans on a made-up 6% slice.
